who: Historian of African American women, University of Maryland; doctorate Kent State, 1994.

evidence.says: Authority for Elsa Barkley Brown cites Black Women in America and identifies her with the University of Michigan history department.
Records her Kent State doctorate in 1994, Michigan faculty service in 1991–1997, subsequent Maryland appointment, and co-editorship of Black Women in America.
Mary-Elizabeth Murphy lists a Maryland history PhD in spring 2012 and dissertation advisor Elsa Barkley Brown.

notes: Matching publication, institutional career, doctorate and named student establish the LC match.

who: Jeffrey S. Brown, historian of twentieth-century US intellectual and cultural history at UNB; PhD history, Rochester.

evidence.says: UNB identifies Jeffrey S. Brown, a Rochester history PhD who joined the department in 2002 and supervises twentieth-century US intellectual and cultural history.
Brent Clowater’s August 2021 history dissertation names Jeffrey S. Brown as supervisor.
The authority for Brown, Jeffrey S. cites CIW (2002), with no university or degree information connecting it to the UNB historian.

notes: Supervisor identity is established, but the reviewed candidate authority records did not provide a reliable connection to him. Shared name or initials alone are insufficient.

who: Historian of African-Atlantic cultures, formerly Southern Illinois University Carbondale; doctorate Georgia, 2004.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Ras Michael Brown of Southern Illinois University, Carbondale, as author of African-Atlantic Cultures and the South Carolina Lowcountry.
Lists Gregory Matthew Carter’s Historical Studies doctorate, the dissertation Do for Do Ain’t No Obeah, and Ras Michael Brown as advisor.
Georgia’s graduate alumni record gives completion in 2004 and the dissertation Crossing Kalunga: West-Central Africans and their Cultural Influence in the South Carolina-Georgia Lowcountry.

notes: LC institution and field match; the SIU commencement record directly confirms the listed student.

who: Winfield J. Burggraaff, historian of Latin America at Missouri; doctorate history, New Mexico, 1967.

evidence.says: Authority cites The Venezuelan Armed Forces (1972), whose jacket identifies Winfield J. Burggraaff as a member of Missouri’s history department.
Missouri identifies Winfield J. Burggraaff as professor emeritus with research area Latin America.
New Mexico records his doctoral history dissertation Civil-Military Relations in Venezuela: 1935–1959, dated June 2, 1967.

notes: The authority, faculty record and exact doctorate agree.

who: Thomas L. Bushell, historian at Michigan State; PhD Northwestern, 1959.

evidence.says: Michigan State’s 1971 commencement lists George Abbott Colburn’s dissertation on T. M. Healy and names Thomas L. Bushell, associate professor, as major professor.
Authority for T. L. (Thomas L.) Bushell cites The Sage of Salisbury and an IEN database record for a 1959 PhD thesis of that title.
Michigan State’s January 1975 minutes identify Thomas L. Bushell as associate professor of history.

notes: Full name, exact student and institution establish the supervisor; the authority’s 1959 thesis corroborates the doctorate.

who: Elizabeth Alice Clement, historian of gender and sexuality at Utah; PhD Pennsylvania, 1998.

Authority for Elizabeth Alice Clement cites Trick or Treat (1998).

who: Patrick T. Conley, historian of Rhode Island and constitutional history at Providence College; PhD Notre Dame.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Patrick T. (Patrick Thomas) Conley as professor of history at Providence College and cites his Rhode Island constitutional convention collections.
Providence history faculty recommendations identify Conley’s teaching there from 1963 through 1994 and his Notre Dame PhD, stated as 1970.
Notre Dame archival index lists Patrick T. Conley with PhD 1970.

notes: Authority affiliation covers both students’ years; degree institution and year agree with the supplied doctorate.
